scores.question: What is the trend in Meta's capex over the last four quarters, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026?

scores.answer:
Meta's quarterly capex rose overall, from $18,829M in Q3 2025 to $30,116M in Q2 2026 [1][2]. It dipped once, in Q1 2026, so the trend is up but not monotonic.
- Q3 2025 to Q4 2025: $18,829M to $21,383M, up 13.56% [1][3].
- Q4 2025 to Q1 2026: $21,383M to $18,997M, down 11.16% [3][4].
- Q1 2026 to Q2 2026: $18,997M to $30,116M, up 58.53% [2][4].
- Overall, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026: up 59.94% [1][2].
The gap between the highest quarter (Q2 2026, $30,116M) and the lowest (Q3 2025, $18,829M) is $11,287M [1][2].
The four quarters are FY2025Q3 through FY2026Q2 because Meta's fiscal year ends December 31 and its latest reported quarter is FY2026Q2 [5].

scores.question: According to Nvidia's 10-Q MD&A for fiscal Q2 2027, what drove the growth in Data Center revenue?
scores.answer:
Nvidia's 10-Q MD&A attributes the growth in Data Center revenue to the ramp of its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure [1]. Data Center revenue was $89.0 billion, up 117% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially [1]. Within that, Hyperscale revenue more than doubled year over year and rose 13% sequentially on the strength of Blackwell Ultra, while ACIE revenue rose 138% year over year, driven by end-demand from AI natives, enterprises, and sovereign customers, as well as hyperscalers using AI clouds [1].

Sources:
[1] NVDA 10-Q FY2027Q2, Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, characters 84229-86247: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm

scores.question: What does Tesla's 10-K say in its risk factors about depending on Elon Musk?
scores.answer:
Tesla's 10-K risk factors state that the company is highly dependent on Elon Musk, its Technoking and Chief Executive Officer. The FY2024 10-K says: "We are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer" [1]. It adds that Mr. Musk "does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla" and holds management positions at other companies, including Space Exploration Technologies Corp. [1]. The key-personnel factor repeats the dependence and notes that none of its key employees is bound by an employment agreement for a specific term [2].
The FY2023 10-K contains the same language [3][4].
I could not confirm from the FY2025 10-K search result whether this wording is unchanged, because that passage did not appear in it.

Sources:
[1] TSLA 10-K FY2024Q4, ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS, characters 93839-96152: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828025003063/tsla-20241231.htm
